items.content_html:
Part of #574149.

These CMake packages install a desktop entry, but they do not install the AppStream metainfo file that upstream supplies in the source. This PR installs the upstream file to share/metainfo. Software centers and search sites use this file to show descriptions and screenshots.

There is one commit for each package. Most commits add one install -Dm644 line to postInstall or to the custom installPhase. Some commits do more:

  • inochi2d: the change is in the shared generic.nix, so it applies to inochi-session and inochi-creator. I built only inochi-session, because the buildPhase of inochi-creator fails on master.
  • chatterino2: the change is in the shared common.nix, so it applies to chatterino7 too.
  • anilibria-winmaclinux, chatterino2, furnace, notepad-next and tic-80: postInstall had only a Darwin part. The commit adds a Linux part, and nixfmt indents the Darwin part again.
  • tev: sets the upstream CMake option -DTEV_CREATE_METAINFO=1.
  • gittyup: sets the upstream CMake option GENERATE_APPDATA.
  • far2l: CMake generates the file with Python markdown, so the commit adds it to nativeBuildInputs.
  • furnace: upstream CMake generates the file only from a git checkout, because it adds the releases from the git tags. The commit installs the template without releases.
  • dolphin-emu: installs the file that CMake generates in the build directory, as the upstream Flatpak manifest does. The commit removes the generated release, because its date comes from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (1980-01-01).
  • pcsx2: the upstream file is a template. The commit removes the release line, because its date comes from git, and sets the commit hash to the source tag.
  • monero-gui: the commit removes the template release line, because it is not valid XML.
  • odamex: also installs the releases file to share/metainfo/releases.
  • jazz2, media-downloader and nvidia-system-monitor-qt: upstream CMake installs the file only in Flatpak builds. These builds also change the behavior of the program, so the commit installs the file manually.
  • beamerpresenter and eiskaltdcpp: the upstream CMake option INSTALL_METAINFO installs a wrong file name or a second file with the same ID, so the commit installs the file manually.
  • eiskaltdcpp, furnace, gittyup, jazz2, js8call, neovim-unwrapped, rclone-browser and satdump: the upstream file name does not contain the component ID, so the commit installs it as <id>.metainfo.xml.

I built each package and checked that its share/metainfo output contains the file.

Desktop entry names

In these packages, <launchable type="desktop-id"> in the metainfo file is not the name of the desktop entry that the package installs. Most of these are Flatpak files. The metainfo is still useful without a match, for example for screenshots on search.nixos.org. I did not rename the desktop entries, because a rename can break user configuration such as mimeapps.list. Maintainers can decide this for each package.

mcontrolcenter and rclone-browser: the metainfo file has no <launchable> element.

Upstream validation problems

appstreamcli validate --no-net reports these errors and warnings in the upstream files. I did not change the files, except for the release lines above:

  • anilibria-winmaclinux: metainfo-localized-description-tag
  • beamerpresenter: description-para-markup-invalid
  • dolphin-emu: cid-domain-not-lowercase
  • m8c: web-url-expected
  • mcontrolcenter and rclone-browser: desktop-app-launchable-missing
  • satdump: metadata-license-invalid
  • odamex: an invalid date in the releases file (warning)
  • openomf: developer-id-invalid (warning)

Packages not in this PR

  • edb, qelectrotech and teeworlds: the upstream file uses the old AppData format (<application> root), and appstreamcli rejects it with metainfo-ancient.
  • dolphin-emu-primehack: the source contains the unchanged Dolphin metainfo, which describes a different app.
  • transmission_4-qt: upstream has metainfo only for the GTK app.

Claude helped to write the code, the commit messages and this PR description.

items.content_html:
Lock mimalloc and cadical pins for lean4 in cmake-content.json (normal fetchFromGitHub FODs) and add passthru.updateScript so r-ryantm / update.nix can bump lean and refresh the lock.

Closes #536990.

What changed

  • cmake-content.json — lock for mimalloc + cadical (owner/repo/tag/hash)
  • Offline mimalloc:
    • Lean ≤4.30 (ExternalProject): rewrite git clone → SOURCE_DIR FOD
    • Lean ≥4.31 (FetchContent): FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_MIMALLOC + FETCHCONTENT_FULLY_DISCONNECTED
    • stage/runtime paths that expect LEAN_BINARY_DIR/../mimalloc/... pointed at the FOD
  • Drop mimalloc.patch
  • cadical package version tracks lock tag (rel-2.1.2 → nixpkgs 2.1.2); add that hash to cadical’s version map
  • passthru.updateScript:
    1. gitUpdater with rev-prefix = "v" and ignoredVersions = "-rc"
    2. update-cmake-content.py: EP regex first, then FetchContent dependency provider (FC wins on name clash); sets NIX_PATH=nixpkgs=<checkout> so nix-prefetch-github works without host channels
  • Bump 4.30.0 → 4.31.0 as the first update exercising this path (upstream pins unchanged: mimalloc v2.2.3, cadical rel-2.1.2)

Why

lean4 had no updateScript, so the bot never opened version bumps. mimalloc/cadical must stay aligned with upstream CMake pins; the lock + second update step refresh those FODs when lean’s src moves.

Testing notes (draft)

Evidence on this machine (x86_64-linux), not a full lean4 package build:

  • nix-instantiate -A lean4 succeeds for 4.31.0
  • content FODs for mimalloc + cadical fetch
  • update-cmake-content.py succeeds with broken host NIX_PATH (lock rewrite)
  • nix-shell maintainers/scripts/update.nix --argstr package lean4 → 4.30.0 → 4.31.0, lock keeps both deps
  • Full nixpkgs-review pr 537536 on x86_64-linux: lean4 built (see review comment)

items.title: openssl: fix cmake files generation

items.content_html:
This PR introduces an option dontExecuteCMake for cmakeConfigurePhase provided by cmake's main setup hook.

When set to 1 (from the Nix Language true), cmakeConfigurePhase will omit the actual cmake configuring execution, but both cmakeEntries and cmakeFlags will still be populated, padded by defult values.

Setting dontExecuteCMake as 1 also defauts separateCMakeEntries to 1, dropping the compatibility behaviour of filling cmakeFlags with D-flags from cmakeEntries.

Using such variable, this PR also provides cmake/tests/test-setup-hook.nix (attached to pkgs as cmake.passthru.tests.setup-hook-tests) for unit-testing cmake/setup-hook.sh.

Additionally, developers can build test-setup-hook.nix without lengthy rebuilds by

nix-build --no-out-link pkgs/by-name/cm/cmake/test/test-setup-hook.nix --arg pkgs "import <nixpkgs> { }" --arg lib "import <nixpkgs/lib>" cmakeFlags-structured-jq

or

nix build --no-link -L -f pkgs/by-name/cm/cmake/tests/test-setup-hook.nix --arg lib "import <nixpkgs/lib>" --arg pkgs "import <nixpkgs> { }"

Closes #296551

items.content_html:
This PR provides structural access to the CMake flags specifying CMake variable cache entries.

If applied, we'll be able to do

{
  stdenv,
  cmake,
}:
stdenv.mkDerivation {
  __structuredAttrs = true;
  nativeBuildInputs = [ cmake ];
  cmakeEntries = {
    CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE = "RelWithDebInfo";
    WITH_PYTHON_BINDINGS = false;
  };
}

Aside from

{
  lib,
  stdenv,
  cmake,
}:
stdenv.mkDerivation {
  nativeBuildInputs = [ cmake ];
  cmakeFlags = [
    (lib.cmakeFeature "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE" "RelWithDebInfo")
    (lib.cmakeBool "WITH_PYTHON_BINDINGS" false)
  ];
}

items.content_html:
Description of changes

#245527 PR author ran into the issue (#144170) where many programs expect CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR & co. to be a relative path, but NixOS sets it to an absolute path. Fedora used to do the same until 2012, but ran into the same issue so it doesn't do that anymore.

Leaving aside whether this should be reconsidered like Fedora did, the #245527 PR author saw the warning about //nix being in a .pc file, so they fixed the code to use CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_LIBDIR. This got rid of the warning, but the .cmake files still contained //nix. This PR adds a warning for }//nix in .cmake files as well (maybe //nix check would make more sense since it's comparatively less likely that it would be }//nix in .cmake files).

Description

The openjpeg package has two outputs, out and dev. The CMake files should be placed at the dev output, but happens to go to the out output due to the way upstream CMake file find the library directory.

This PR guides the openjpeg CMake file installation to the correct output by patching the CMake file responsible for the installation.

This PR also makes openjpeg more overridable by adopting stdenv.mkDerivation's fixed-point arguments support. If merged, users can override doCheck, outputs, and version directly, and test-data via passthru.test-data.
